title: Audio to structured incident reports
purpose: Evaluate whether the GAIK Solution Configuration Wizard captures the fixed scenario, chooses and configures a valid GAIK solution, generates a valid solution package, and produces an executable PoC.

protocol.output_directory_policy: Write the wizard output to the run-specific generated_package directory, or copy the complete unmodified output there after the run. No absolute path is stored in run metadata.
protocol.confirmation_policy: At every routine confirmation before original PoC execution, answer Yes and proceed without changes.
protocol.unexpected_question_answer: Not specified for this evaluation. If a value is required, record it as an explicit assumption for user confirmation.
protocol.po_c_policy: Execute the original wizard-generated PoC without editing its source files. Environment variables and credentials may be supplied externally. EQ4 is permanently based on this original execution.

recovery_policy.trigger: The original PoC does not execute successfully.
recovery_policy.feedback_scope: Return recorded execution evidence to the wizard without adding corrective code or new requirements.
recovery_policy.stopping_rule: Stop after the first successful execution or after the third unsuccessful refinement.

reported_values.1-3: PoC executed successfully after the stated number of refinement attempts.
reported_values.N/A: PoC never executed successfully after three refinement attempts.

EQ1.oracle_value: Field technician
EQ1.accepted_semantics: A field, facility, or maintenance technician creates the report.

EQ1.oracle_value: Technician manually enters fault information into the maintenance system.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Manual entry into a maintenance or maintenance-management system is described.

EQ1.oracle_value: Manual reporting is slow and can omit details.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Both reporting delay/effort and missing/incomplete details are captured.

EQ1.oracle_value: Maintenance supervisor
EQ1.accepted_semantics: A supervisor or equivalent maintenance reviewer checks the ticket.

EQ1.oracle_value: Faster reporting with fewer missing details.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The proposed solution reduces reporting effort/time and improves completeness.

EQ1.oracle_value: Voice message/audio file
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The solution accepts a spoken report or audio recording.

EQ1.oracle_value: Finnish (fi)
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Finnish is explicitly represented, with fi accepted as the language code.

EQ1.oracle_value: One speaker; diarization not required.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The report is single-speaker and diarization is false, absent because unnecessary, or explicitly not required.

EQ1.oracle_value: Structured maintenance ticket in JSON-compatible form.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The final machine-readable output is a structured maintenance incident/fault ticket.

EQ1.oracle_value: reporter_name
EQ1.accepted_semantics: A field records the reporting technician or reporter identity.

EQ1.oracle_value: asset_identifier
EQ1.accepted_semantics: A field identifies the affected asset, equipment, or component.

EQ1.oracle_value: location; required
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Location is present and required.

EQ1.oracle_value: fault_description; required
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The broken/fault condition is present as a required description field.

EQ1.oracle_value: urgency; required
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Urgency, priority, or severity is present and required.

EQ1.parameter: Output field: observation date and time
EQ1.oracle_value: observation_date and observation_time, or one equivalent timestamp field
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The time of observation is captured, either as separate date/time fields or one timestamp.

EQ1.oracle_value: actions_taken
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The ticket records any immediate actions already performed.

EQ1.oracle_value: Leave missing values empty or unknown; never invent a value.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The output or prompt specifies that unstated values remain blank/unknown and must not be fabricated.

EQ1.oracle_value: Flag missing or uncertain fields for supervisor review.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Missing, ambiguous, low-confidence, or uncertain fields are surfaced to the reviewer.

EQ1.oracle_value: Original transcript is available to the supervisor.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The reviewer can inspect the transcript or equivalent source evidence.

EQ1.oracle_value: Supervisor reviews before transfer.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: A mandatory human review occurs after ticket generation and before external-system transfer.

EQ1.oracle_value: Approve or return for correction.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The supervisor can approve and can reject/return/rework the generated ticket.

EQ1.oracle_value: Production target is the maintenance management system; PoC exports approved JSON and does not implement the live API.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The maintenance system is the intended target, while the PoC is limited to file/JSON output.

EQ1.oracle_value: Audio may contain employee identity and internal facility details.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Personal data and internal/sensitive facility information are recognized.

EQ1.oracle_value: Allowed
EQ1.accepted_semantics: External model APIs are permitted and local-only processing is not required.

EQ1.oracle_value: Do not retain raw audio after processing in the PoC.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The PoC does not persist input audio beyond processing.

EQ1.oracle_value: Approved ticket and supervisor approval decision may be retained; no exact retention period.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Structured approved output and approval evidence may be stored, without inventing a retention duration.

EQ1.oracle_value: Command-line interface
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The generated PoC can be run from a CLI.

EQ1.oracle_value: Field technicians and the maintenance supervisor are the only required PoC participants; the voice report is internal and has no external party.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The required actors are the technician and supervisor, and no external sender or additional business stakeholder is introduced as confirmed scope.

EQ1.oracle_value: Faster reporting, fewer missing details, a supervisor-verifiable ticket, and successful execution over the supplied fixture; no numerical improvement threshold.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Success includes the stated qualitative business outcome and runnable single-fixture PoC without inventing a quantified target.

EQ1.oracle_value: Finnish transcription errors; incorrect asset, location, fault, or urgency values; unsupported values; transfer without supervisor approval.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The risk description covers transcription/extraction error, unsupported data, and bypass of the review gate.

EQ1.oracle_value: An internal technician records or uploads Finnish audio; extracted free-text values remain Finnish, while JSON keys and canonical urgency labels are English.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The solution distinguishes Finnish source/free text from English machine-readable keys and canonical labels.

EQ1.oracle_value: Finnish facility names and alphanumeric room/asset identifiers may occur; identifiers such as P-17 and B2 must be preserved exactly; no fixed glossary.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The design preserves domain identifiers and does not claim a supplied glossary.

EQ1.oracle_value: Provider remains configurable; no exact provider, model, temperature, or transcription model is user-specified.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The specification records configurability or no preference and does not turn an implementation default into a confirmed requirement.

EQ1.oracle_value: Final machine-readable JSON ticket; transcript and uncertainty information as review evidence; no formatted PDF, HTML, or DOCX report.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: JSON is the required final format and formatted-report output is explicitly unnecessary.

EQ1.oracle_value: MaintenanceTicket
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The target output schema is named MaintenanceTicket or a clearly equivalent maintenance-ticket schema.

EQ1.oracle_value: Strings for reporter_name, asset_identifier, location, fault_description, urgency, and observation_time; date for observation_date; lists of strings for actions_taken and uncertain_fields. location, fault_description, and urgency are required; other fields are optional.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: All named fields have semantically compatible types and the required/optional split is preserved.

EQ1.oracle_value: urgency is low, medium, or high; observation_date uses YYYY-MM-DD; observation_time uses HH:MM.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The controlled urgency vocabulary and date/time formats are represented in the schema, prompt, or validation rules.

EQ1.oracle_value: A numerical confidence score is not required; component-supplied confidence may be included only as supplementary evidence.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The design does not make numeric confidence mandatory and keeps uncertainty reviewable.

EQ1.oracle_value: Required keys must exist; constrained formats and urgency values must be respected; values must be grounded in the message; missing or uncertain values remain null/unknown and are listed in uncertain_fields.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The generated validation rules cover structure, controlled values/formats, grounding, and missing-value handling.

EQ1.oracle_value: Technician submits audio; AI creates a ticket and review evidence; supervisor approves or returns it; only approved JSON proceeds. There are no external parties or additional decision branches.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: Roles, hand-offs, manual review, rejection/resubmission, and the approval condition are present without unsupported branches.

EQ1.oracle_value: Run the supplied Finnish audio fixture; require successful exit, parseable non-empty JSON, required-field coverage, semantic preservation of fixture facts, and no unsupported values; no numerical threshold.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The evaluation plan defines the fixture and observable acceptance checks without inventing a benchmark threshold.

EQ1.oracle_value: External APIs are allowed; raw audio is not retained; approved ticket and approval decision may be retained; authentication, production RBAC, and a full audit-log implementation are outside PoC scope.
EQ1.accepted_semantics: The specification captures the stated PoC data-handling boundaries and does not add production security implementations as confirmed requirements.

EQ1_diagnostics.oracle_value: The provider must remain configurable; no exact provider or model was supplied.
EQ1_diagnostics.accepted_semantics: Configurability is preserved. Any concrete provider/model is marked as an explicit assumption or implementation default, not as a user-confirmed requirement.

EQ1_diagnostics.oracle_value: No exact retention period was supplied.
EQ1_diagnostics.accepted_semantics: No exact duration is silently presented as user-confirmed; not_specified or an explicit assumption is acceptable.

EQ1_diagnostics.parameter: Unsupported SLA, volume, budget, or deployment commitment
EQ1_diagnostics.oracle_value: No SLA, throughput, budget, or deployment topology was supplied.
EQ1_diagnostics.accepted_semantics: Any concrete value is marked as an explicit assumption rather than a confirmed requirement.

EQ2.accepted_semantics: The use case is classified as knowledge capture.
The GAIK AudioToStructuredData module is selected as the end-to-end solution for audio-to-structured-data.
The Finnish language is configured at technical or component level.
The module/transcriber enables the Finnish-tuned enhanced transcript behavior.

EQ2.oracle_value: The PoC invokes AudioToStructuredData once and does not independently invoke its subsumed Transcriber, TranscriptEnhancer, SchemaGenerator, or DataExtractor pipeline.
EQ2.accepted_semantics: Components may be named for traceability or internal decomposition, but the executable design must not run a duplicate standalone pipeline alongside the selected module.

EQ2.oracle_value: A schema/requirements artifact defines all required maintenance-ticket fields.
EQ2.accepted_semantics: Schema and extraction requirements are connected to the audio-to-structured module and cover the EQ1 output fields.

EQ2.oracle_value: Human review follows structured extraction and precedes maintenance-system transfer.
EQ2.accepted_semantics: Workflow ordering and dependencies enforce the review gate in the required position.

EQ2.oracle_value: Supervisor receives the structured ticket, uncertainty/missing-field information, and transcript evidence.
EQ2.accepted_semantics: The review step has enough artifacts to verify and correct the ticket.

EQ2.oracle_value: CLI accepts audio and saves JSON; live API integration is not required.
EQ2.accepted_semantics: The generated runtime and package match the agreed PoC scope.

EQ3.oracle_value: generated_package/use_case.blueprint.json exists, is non-empty, and parses as JSON.
The GAIK Solution Wizard validator returns exit code 0 with no blocking errors.
Step inputs/outputs reference declared artifacts; generated artifacts have valid producers; dependencies are resolvable.
workflow.mmd exists, is non-empty, and contains the workflow step labels or identifiers.
workflow.bpmn is well-formed XML and its mapping or element identifiers cover the blueprint workflow.
poc/ contains an executable entrypoint, dependency declaration, configuration/example environment, extraction prompt, and output schema or schema-generation assets.
docs/ contains at least one non-empty use-case-specific document and the PoC contains usage instructions.
The blueprint traceability data connects selected module/component decisions to stated requirements.

EQ4.oracle_value: For the original unmodified PoC, the declared setup or import command completes with exit code 0.
The original unmodified generated PoC processes incident_report_fi.wav and exits with code 0.
The original unmodified PoC generates a new non-empty JSON ticket that parses successfully.
The original unmodified PoC output preserves the expected incident facts in expected_ticket.json and does not silently invent unsupported ticket facts.

EQ1.formula: Yes verdicts for EQ1-R rows / total EQ1-R rows

EQ2.formula: Yes verdicts for EQ2-C rows / total EQ2-C rows

EQ3.formula: A run passes only if every mandatory EQ3-P check is Yes; passed runs / 2

EQ4.formula: A run passes only if every mandatory EQ4-X check for the original unmodified PoC is Yes; passed runs / 2

recovery_diagnostic.formula: Record the first successful execution: 0 for original success, 1-3 for success after that many refinements, and N/A when all three refinements fail.
recovery_diagnostic.reporting: Report initially successful runs, runs recovered within three refinements, and runs that never executed successfully.

scoring.two_run_aggregation: For EQ1 and EQ2, pool Yes verdicts across both runs and divide by the pooled number of scored checks. For EQ3 and EQ4, divide the number of passing runs by two.

verdict_policy.semantic_matching: The LLM may align semantically equivalent wording and identify evidence, but it must not enter the final verdict. The evaluator reviews the side-by-side evidence and enters Yes or No.
verdict_policy.missing_requirement: If an oracle requirement is absent, the generated-value cell states NOT FOUND, the evidence cell lists the searched sources/paths, and the evaluator enters No. This keeps omitted requirements in the denominator.
verdict_policy.evidence_rule: Every verdict cell must have adjacent evidence that identifies the source file and a concrete excerpt, path, command result, or parser/validator result.
